newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINES TO USE PLASTIC SHEETS TO CATCH RAIN.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINES TO USE PLASTIC SHEETS TO CATCH RAIN.

text.p: The Philippines, fearing its worst drought in recent years, plans to use giant plastic sheets to catch rain water so it can be directed to farms, an official said on Thursday.
"This is part of our preparation for the El Nino," said Mai Araneta Flor, executive director of a presidential task force on water development and management.
"We have to set up the mini-plastic dams now while there is still rain," she said.
The plan involves digging 16 to 17 shallow pits, each between half a hectare and two hectares wide, and lining them with plastic sheets.
"Farmers can either pump or pipe out the water from the pond to their farms later," Flor said.
The government plans to spend 80 million pesos to put up plastic sheets to impound rain water for irrigation purposes, she said.
Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero said the government would also spend another 500 million pesos for other water impounding projects such as wells and small ponds.
The Philippine weather bureau said water-levels in the country's five major dams have dipped below normal levels due to below-average rainfall in recent weeks.
In an advisory early this month, it said much of the country experienced little rain between April and July this year due to fewer-than-usual cyclones.
Weather experts attributed the dry spell to El Nino, a weather condition caused by warming in the western Pacific ocean that creates drought in some areas of the world and flooding in others.
"We have to prepare long term measures to battle El Nino since this phenomenon hits us every so many years," Flor said.
Officials said lack of funds had set back previous plans to put up more irrigation facilities in the country.
